input.system:
You are a friendly, precise sports dietitian. A deterministic engine has already computed this person's daily nutrition targets, each with the reason behind it. Your job is to explain the plan in plain English so the person understands why the numbers are what they are and how to hit them.

Rules:
- Explain, never change. Quote the targets exactly as given, with their units. Do not propose different numbers, do not round them further, and do not suggest eating below any target.
- Mention the energy target, the protein target and at least one other number in the paragraphs.
- Write in the second person, warm but not gushing. No hype, no medical claims, no diagnosis.
- Respect the diet pattern, allergies and dislikes: never suggest a food that conflicts with them (a vegan gets B12 from fortified foods or a supplement, not meat).
- If the plan says professional guidance is advised, say so gently in a caveat.
- Keep the whole answer under 200 words.

Output shape:
- headline: one sentence that sums up the plan, with the energy target in it.
- paragraphs: 2 to 4 short paragraphs (energy and why; protein and why; fat, carbs and fibre; anything else that matters for this person).
- key_habits: exactly 3 concrete, specific habits for this person and their diet pattern.
- caveats: 0 to 3 short notes (for example a lower water target on rest days, or a note from the engine).
input.user:
PERSON
- Sex: Male, age 28
- Height: 178 cm, weight: 75 kg
- Goal: Gain muscle at a lean gain pace (about 0.25 kg a week, mostly muscle), goal weight 80 kg
- Activity: High (hard training 6 to 7 days a week)
- Training: Combat sports, 6 days a week
- Diet pattern: Omnivore
- Allergies or intolerances: none
- Dislikes: liver
- Units the person uses: metric

ENGINE SUMMARY
- Basal metabolic rate 1728 kcal (Mifflin-St Jeor), activity multiplier 1.725, maintenance 2980 kcal, adjustment +270 kcal a day
- Protein basis: 2.0 g per kg of 75 kg
- Water on rest days: 2750 ml

TARGETS (value, kind, then the reason)
- Energy: 3250 kcal (aim for). 2980 kcal to maintain (1728 kcal basal by Mifflin-St Jeor, times 1.725 for high activity), plus 275 kcal a day for a lean gain pace of about 0.25 kg a week (7700 kcal per kg).
- Protein: 150 g (aim for). 2.0 g/kg × 75 kg for a lean gain, plus 0.2 g/kg for combat sports.
- Carbs: 460 g (aim for). What is left after protein and fat: about 6.1 g/kg.
- Fat: 90 g (aim for). 25% of energy, above the 0.5 g/kg floor of 38 g.
- Fibre: 45 g (at least). 14 g per 1000 kcal, at least 25 g and at most 45 g.
- Added sugar: 81 g (at most). Under 10% of energy, the WHO limit for added sugars.
- Saturated fat: 36 g (at most). Under 10% of energy.
- Sodium: 2300 mg (at most). 2300 mg upper limit. Heavy sweaters may need more on hard training days.
- Water: 3250 ml (aim for). 35 ml per kg plus 500 ml per training hour: 3250 ml on training days, 2750 ml on rest days.
- Alcohol: 0 drinks (at most). Zero is the target. 2 standard drinks (10 g of alcohol each) in a day counts as over.
- Potassium: 3400 mg (at least). Adequate intake for men aged 19 to 30.
- Calcium: 1000 mg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Iron: 8 mg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Magnesium: 400 mg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Zinc: 11 mg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Vitamin A: 900 mcg RAE (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Vitamin C: 90 mg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Vitamin D: 15 mcg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Vitamin B12: 2.4 mcg (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Folate: 400 mcg DFE (at least). RDA for men aged 19 to 30.
- Vegetables: 6 serves (at least). Australian Dietary Guidelines for men aged 19 to 30. One serve is 75 g cooked vegetables or legumes, or 1 cup salad, or half a medium potato.
- Fruit: 2 serves (at least). Australian Dietary Guidelines for men aged 19 to 30. One serve is 150 g fresh fruit, or 1 medium piece, or 30 g dried.
- Whole grains: 6 serves (at least). Australian Dietary Guidelines for men aged 19 to 30. One serve is 1 slice wholegrain bread, half a cup cooked wholegrain rice, pasta or oats, 30 g wholegrain cereal.
- Protein foods: 3 serves (at least). Australian Dietary Guidelines for men aged 19 to 30. One serve is 65 g cooked lean meat, 80 g cooked poultry, 100 g cooked fish, 2 large eggs, 150 g cooked legumes or tofu, 30 g nuts or seeds.
- Dairy or alternatives: 2.5 serves (at least). Australian Dietary Guidelines for men aged 19 to 30. One serve is 250 ml milk or fortified plant milk, 200 g yoghurt, 40 g hard cheese.
- Legumes: 1 serves (for information). Shown for information, not scored. One serve is 150 g cooked legumes (counts toward protein foods and vegetables too).
- Nuts and seeds: 1 serves (for information). Shown for information, not scored. One serve is 30 g.

response.headline: Your lean-gain target is 3250 kcal per day to support hard combat-sports training and gradual muscle gain.
paragraphs: Your 3250 kcal target comes from an estimated 2980 kcal maintenance need plus 275 kcal for a lean gain pace of about 0.25 kg per week. This gives you enough fuel to train 6 days a week while aiming to add weight steadily rather than aggressively.

Your protein target is 150 g per day, based on your 75 kg body weight and the extra demands of combat sports. Spread it across meals using foods you tolerate and like, such as lean meat, poultry, fish, eggs, dairy, tofu, legumes, nuts and seeds, while avoiding liver since you dislike it.

Carbs are set at 460 g per day to refill glycogen and support repeated hard sessions. Fat is 90 g per day, with saturated fat capped at 36 g. Fibre is 45 g at least, helped by the targets of 6 serves vegetables, 2 serves fruit and 6 serves whole grains.

Hydration matters with your training load: aim for 3250 ml water on training days. Keep added sugar to 81 g at most, sodium to 2300 mg at most unless heavy sweating changes your needs, and alcohol to 0 drinks.
key_habits: Build each main meal around a protein food serve, a large carb portion such as rice, pasta, oats, potatoes or bread, and vegetables.
Use training-friendly carbs around sessions, such as oats, fruit, yoghurt, sandwiches, rice bowls or pasta meals.
Include 2.5 serves dairy or alternatives daily, plus nuts, seeds or olive oil to help reach 90 g fat without relying on saturated fat.
caveats: On rest days, your water target is lower: 2750 ml.
Heavy sweaters may need more sodium on hard training days.
